label: thm:A
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:A}
For every $n$ and $D>0$ there is a constant $C(n,D)$ such that every
closed Riemannian $n$-manifold $(M,g)$ satisfying
\[
        \mathop{\rm Ric}\geq -(n-1),\qquad \mathop{\rm Diam}(M)\leq D
\]
satisfies
\[
        \sum_{i=0}^n\widetilde\beta_i(M)\leq C(n,D).
\]
head: environment
name: Bounded Betti number theorem

title: Definition
body_md:
The bounded part of $H^i(M;{\bf R})$ is
\[
       \widetilde H^i(M)=\mathop{\rm Im}\{c^i:\widehat H^i(M;{\bf R})\to H^i(M;{\bf R})\}.
\]
Its dimension
\[
       \widetilde\beta_i(M)=\dim\widetilde H^i(M)
\]
is the bounded Betti number.
head: environment

label: prop:duality
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:duality}
If $\alpha\in\widetilde H^i(M)$ and $z\in H_i(M;{\bf R})$, then
\[
       |\langle\alpha,z\rangle|
       \leq \|\alpha\|_\infty\,\|z\|_1.
\]
In particular, every bounded ordinary cohomology class vanishes on
every homology class whose $\ell^1$-seminorm is zero.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
This viewpoint also explains why $\widetilde H^i(M)$ can behave very differently
from both $\widehat H^i(M)$ and $H^i(M)$.  The comparison map can have a large
kernel and a small image, or the ordinary cohomology group itself can
be too small to receive the bounded classes.
head: environment

title: Example
body_md:
If $\pi_1(M)$ is amenable, then
\[
        \widehat H^i(M;{\bf R})=0\qquad (i\geq1)
\]
in the standard setting of bounded cohomology.  Consequently
\[
        \widetilde H^i(M)=0,\qquad \widetilde\beta_i(M)=0\quad (i\geq1).
\]
In particular, tori and closed manifolds with virtually nilpotent
fundamental group have trivial bounded part in positive degrees.
head: environment
name: Amenable fundamental group

title: Example
body_md:
For a closed negatively curved manifold, the comparison map is
surjective in degrees $i\geq2$ by the classical bounded-cohomological
results used in the original paper.  Thus
\[
        \widetilde H^i(M)=H^i(M;{\bf R}),\qquad
        \widetilde\beta_i(M)=\beta_i(M),\quad i\geq2.
\]
This represents the opposite extreme from the amenable case.
head: environment
name: Closed negatively curved manifolds

title: Example
body_md:
Let $M$ be a closed hyperbolic integral homology $3$-sphere.  Its
bounded cohomology can be nontrivial in degree two, whereas
\[
        H^2(M;{\bf R})=0.
\]
Therefore
\[
        \widetilde H^2(M)=0
\]
although $\widehat H^2(M;{\bf R})$ is nontrivial.  This example makes clear that
the bounded part is not determined by the size of bounded cohomology
alone.
head: environment
name: Hyperbolic homology $3$-sphere

title: Example
body_md:
Let $N$ be a closed manifold and consider $M=N\times S^1$.
The circle contributes an amenable factor to the fundamental group.
The mapping theorem for bounded cohomology shows that amenable normal
subgroups do not contribute new bounded cohomology.  Nevertheless,
ordinary cohomology acquires the additional classes supplied by the
$S^1$ factor.  Hence the passage from $\widehat H^*(M)$ to $\widetilde H^*(M)$ again
depends on how the bounded classes map into the enlarged ordinary
cohomology.
head: environment
name: Products with an amenable factor

label: thm:KW
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:KW}
For each positive integer $n$, there are constants $\epsilon(n)>0$
and $C(n)>0$ with the following property.  Let $(M^n,g)$ be a complete
Riemannian manifold and suppose that
\[
        \mathop{\rm Ric}_M>-(n-1)
\]
on the metric ball $B_1(p)$.  Then the image of the natural
homomorphism
\[
 \pi_1(B_{\epsilon(n)}(p),p)
       \longrightarrow \pi_1(B_1(p),p)
\]
contains a nilpotent subgroup $N$ of index at most $C(n)$.
Moreover, $N$ admits a nilpotent basis of length at most $n$.
head: environment
name: Kapovitch--Wilking generalized Margulis lemma

title: Remark
body_md:
For a lower sectional curvature bound, related local fundamental group
results were established by Fukaya and Yamaguchi.  A weaker Ricci
curvature version was stated by Cheeger and Colding in connection with
their structure theory for Ricci limit spaces.  Kapovitch and Wilking
gave a complete generalized Margulis lemma under a lower Ricci
curvature bound and, importantly, obtained a uniform bound depending
only on the dimension for the index of the nilpotent subgroup.
head: environment
name: Historical comment

label: cor:amenrad
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:amenrad}
For every positive integer $n$ there is $r(n)>0$ such that, if $M^n$
is complete and
\[
             \mathop{\rm Ric}_M\geq -(n-1),
\]
then, for every $p\in M$, the image of
\[
 \pi_1(B_{r(n)}(p),p)\longrightarrow\pi_1(M,p)
\]
is virtually nilpotent, and hence amenable.
head: environment
name: Uniform amenability radius

title: Proof
body_md:
First suppose that the strict inequality
$\mathop{\rm Ric}_M>-(n-1)$ holds on $B_1(p)$.  Put $r(n)=\epsilon(n)$, where
$\epsilon(n)$ is supplied by Theorem~\ref{thm:KW}.  Let $G_p$ be the
image of
\[
 \pi_1(B_{r(n)}(p),p)\longrightarrow\pi_1(B_1(p),p).
\]
Theorem~\ref{thm:KW} says that $G_p$ is virtually nilpotent.  The image
of $\pi_1(B_{r(n)}(p),p)$ in $\pi_1(M,p)$ is the image of $G_p$ under
the homomorphism induced by $B_1(p)\longrightarrow M$.  It is therefore
a quotient of $G_p$.  A quotient of a virtually nilpotent group is
virtually nilpotent, and every virtually nilpotent group is amenable.

For the non-strict lower bound, replace $g$ temporarily by
$g_2=4g$.  Then
\[
 \mathop{\rm Ric}_{g_2}\geq-{n-1\over 4}g_2>-(n-1)g_2.
\]
Applying the strict case to $g_2$ shows that the image of the
$g$-ball of radius $\epsilon(n)/2$ in $\pi_1(M,p)$ is virtually
nilpotent.  Thus $r(n)=\epsilon(n)/2$ works uniformly.  Notice that
this rescaling does not change any fundamental group or inclusion
homomorphism.
head: environment

label: lem:Ivanov
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:Ivanov}
Let ${\cal U}=\{U_j\}$ be an amenable open covering of $M$ and let
$N({\cal U})$ be its nerve.  Then the comparison map
\[
       \widehat H^*(M;{\bf R})\longrightarrow H^*(M;{\bf R})
\]
factors through $H^*(|N({\cal U})|;{\bf R})$.
Consequently,
\[
       \widetilde\beta_i(M)\leq \dim H^i(|N({\cal U})|;{\bf R}).
\]
head: environment
name: Amenable covering factorization

title: Proof
body_md:
\ 
Fix $n$ and $D$, and let $r=r(n)$ be the radius in
Corollary~\ref{cor:amenrad}.  Decreasing $r$ if necessary, assume that
$r\leq1$.  For every $p\in M$, the image of
$\pi_1(B_r(p),p)$ in $\pi_1(M,p)$ is virtually nilpotent and hence
amenable.

Choose a maximal collection of pairwise disjoint balls
\[
        B(p_j,r/2),\qquad j=1,\ldots,m.
\]
Then the balls $B(p_j,r)$ cover $M$.  Bishop--Gromov relative volume
comparison gives, for each $j$,
\[
 {\mathop{\rm vol} B(p_j,r/2)\over\mathop{\rm vol} M}
 \geq {V_{-1}(r/2)\over V_{-1}(D+1)},
\]
where $V_{-1}(a)$ denotes the volume of an $a$-ball in the simply
connected space of constant curvature $-1$.  Since the small balls are
pairwise disjoint, this gives a uniform bound
\[
        m\leq C_1(n,D).
\]
More precisely,
\[
 m\leq
 \frac{\displaystyle\int_0^{D+1}(\sinh t)^{\,n-1}\,dt}
      {\displaystyle\int_0^{r/2}(\sinh t)^{\,n-1}\,dt}.
\]

Each member of the covering is amenable in $M$.  Let $N$ be its nerve.
Since the covering contains at most $C_1(n,D)$ sets, the total number
of simplices of $N$ is bounded by a constant depending only on $n$ and
$D$.  Hence
\[
        \sum_i\dim H^i(|N|;{\bf R})\leq C_2(n,D).
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:Ivanov}, the comparison map factors through
$H^*(|N|;{\bf R})$, and therefore
\[
        \sum_i\widetilde\beta_i(M)
        \leq\sum_i\dim H^i(|N|;{\bf R})
        \leq C_2(n,D).
\]
This proves the theorem.
\hfill\rule{1.2ex}{1.2ex}\par
head: manual
name: Theorem \refthm:A

label: cor:geometric
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:geometric}
For every positive integer $n$ and every $D>0$, there is a constant
$C=C(n,D)$ such that every closed Riemannian $n$-manifold satisfying
\[
       \mathop{\rm Ric}(M)\geq-(n-1),\qquad \mathop{\rm Diam}(M)\leq D,
\]
satisfies
\[
 \sum_{i=0}^n
 \dim\left(
 H_i(M;{\bf R})/\{z\in H_i(M;{\bf R}):\|z\|_1=0\}
 \right)
 \leq C(n,D).
\]
head: environment
name: Geometric reformulation

title: Remark
body_md:
The passage from the local Kapovitch--Wilking group to the group used
by the amenable covering theorem is exactly the composition
\[
 \pi_1(B_r(p),p)\longrightarrow\pi_1(B_1(p),p)
 \longrightarrow\pi_1(M,p).
\]
The second image is a quotient of the first image.  This quotient
observation, rather than a subgroup argument, is what transfers virtual
nilpotence and amenability to $M$.
head: environment

label: thm:collapse
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:collapse}
Let $X$ be a compact metric space and let $n$ be fixed.  There is
$\delta=\delta(n,X)>0$ such that, for a closed Riemannian
$n$-manifold satisfying
\[
        \mathop{\rm Ric}\geq-(n-1)
\]
and
\[
        d_{GH}(M,X)<\delta,
\]
one has
\[
        \widetilde\beta_i(M)=0\qquad\quad\hbox{for }i>\dim X.
\]
head: environment
